title: Clearance Manifest v0.2: source-text cleaning vectors, at the level of JSON text
description: Language-neutral vectors for clean() (proposal sections 3.1 to 3.5), for SC-2 (valueCleaned is clean(value)) and for SC-3 (ruleContext contains no code point in the removed set). Every input is JSON TEXT, carried as a string, so an implementation feeds it to its own JSON parser and its own escape handling. Escapes inside these texts are significant: an unpaired surrogate escape, a repeated member name and a raw character beside an escape each test something a parser can hide.

format.clean: input is the JSON text of a source value. cleaned is the JSON text of clean(input): null when cleaning merges two member names or the text repeats one. cleanedUtf8 is the UTF-8 encoding of the expected string, in lowercase hex, present when the result is a string. Compare results as JSON values; member order is not significant.
format.valueCleaned: value and valueCleaned are the JSON texts of the two members of rights.sourceApiValue. verdict is ok when valueCleaned is clean(value) as JSON values and rejected otherwise (SC-2). An unpaired surrogate escape in valueCleaned is detected and rejected, never removed (section 3.5).
format.ruleContext: ruleContext is the JSON text of verification.ruleContext. verdict is rejected when it contains a code point in the removed set, an unpaired surrogate escape included (SC-3).

vectors.note: Nothing to remove.
A zero-width space written as an escape is removed.
The same character written raw is removed the same way.
An override, a run of tag characters (raw, outside the BMP) and a zero-width space are all removed.
Tag characters written as surrogate-pair escapes form valid pairs, and the decoded code points are removed.
ZWNJ, ZWJ, a Mongolian free variation selector, the Mongolian vowel separator, TAB and LF are kept.
Persian text: the leading byte-order mark goes, the ZWNJ inside the word stays.
C0 NUL, DELETE and a C1 control are removed.
A raw soft hyphen is removed.
No HTML decoding, no normalisation, no whitespace change; U+FFFC, U+2800, private use and U+2028 are not in the removed set.
U+FFFD written as an escape is a visible character and is kept.
U+FFFD written raw is kept.
An unpaired high-surrogate escape, as a string cut inside an emoji leaves, is removed.
An unpaired high-surrogate escape between letters is removed.
An unpaired low-surrogate escape is removed.
A high escape directly followed by a low escape is a pair and is kept.
Hex digits are case-insensitive.
Removing a character between two halves never joins them: all three go.
A low escape followed by a high escape is not a pair; both go.
The first high escape is unpaired; the second pairs with the low escape.
An escaped backslash followed by 'ud83d' is six visible characters, not an escape.
A raw character is never half of a pair, so the high escape before a raw emoji is unpaired.
Ordinary escapes decode as usual; the trailing unpaired escape goes.
Member names and every string at any depth are cleaned; numbers and null are unchanged.
Numbers, booleans and null are unchanged.
A member name is cleaned like any string.
Two member names that clean to one: the whole value cleans to null.
A merge at any depth makes the whole value null.
The text repeats a member name: null, whichever member a parser would keep.
A repeat with equal values, at depth, is still a repeat.
Equal names in different objects are not a repeat.
A member named __proto__ is an ordinary member and stays.
A merge through a member named __proto__ is a merge.
An unpaired escape in a member name is removed.
Removing an unpaired escape from a name can merge it with another name: null.
valueCleaned is clean(value).
Compared as JSON values: member order is not significant.
A merge gives null, and valueCleaned says so.
A repeated name gives null.
The unpaired escape is gone from valueCleaned.
valueCleaned still contains U+202E.
valueCleaned changes visible text.
A merge resolved to one member instead of null.
value repeats a name, and valueCleaned keeps the last member instead of null.
The text of valueCleaned repeats a name, which clean() never produces.
valueCleaned has U+FFFD where value has an unpaired surrogate escape.
valueCleaned holds an unpaired surrogate escape in place of a real U+FFFD; it is detected, never removed.
valueCleaned joins two halves that clean() removes.
Plain prose.
ZWNJ is not in the removed set.
A valid surrogate-pair escape is an ordinary character.
U+202E is in the removed set.
A raw zero-width space is in the removed set.
An unpaired surrogate escape is in the removed set; it is detected, never removed.
